stories.title: To train robots, AI companies are paying people in India to film themselves doing chores
stories.summary: Men and women across India are being paid to record themselves doing domestic jobs as developers train AI robots to do household chores.

stories.title: WNBA star Nneka Ogwumike has earned a little rest
stories.summary: Nneka Ogwumike's legacy was never in question winning a championship and league MVP within four years. Negotiating the largest collective bargaining agreement in pro sports for the WNBA ensures it.

stories.title: This week in science: sea monsters, long COVID patients' microbiome, elephant carcasses
stories.summary: NPR's science podcast Short Wave brings us stories about the hunting habits of ancient sea monsters, the microbiome of long COVID patients, and how elephant carcasses replenish the savannah.

stories.title: Three years on, Israel still bars foreign journalists from entering Gaza
stories.summary: More than a year into a declared ceasefire in Gaza — and three years into the war — Israel still hasn't allowed foreign media independent access to Gaza.

stories.title: When students learn to 'Speak,' they also learn to listen
stories.summary: NPR's Ailsa Chang talks with Jennifer Tiexiera and Mfaz Mohamed Ali, filmmaker and original oratory competitor, about their documentary, Speak, and the importance of speech clubs in schools.

stories.title: Actor and author Nick Offerman reflects on a place that shaped him
stories.summary: On Wild Card, well-known guests answer the kinds of questions we often think about but don't talk about. Actor and author Nick Offerman reflects on a place that shaped him.
